title: The aggregate value assessment of green stocks in Borsa Istanbul
summary: The intersection of investment decisions and environmental, social, and governance (ESG) considerations is important in the finance literature. This paper explores the aggregate value assessment of green stocks listed on Borsa Istanbul Sustainability Index over brown stocks that are not listed, employing the total efficiency loss (TEL) model. Understanding the performance dynamics of ESG-sensitive portfolios becomes imperative as investors increasingly prioritize sustainability. The study covers the data of the BIST-SI and the BIST100 Index between 2015 and 2023. Our findings indicate a consistent outperformance of green portfolios over brown portfolios, except for the years 2016 and 2022, suggesting that during periods of economic and political instability, external factors may influence investor preferences. In particular, the deviation in these years highlights the sensitivity of ESG investments to both domestic and global shocks, highlighting the importance of considering contextual dynamics in portfolio management. This study contributes to the literature on sustainable finance by providing insights into the relative performance of green portfolios and emphasizing the positive association between ESG considerations and financial outcomes. Furthermore, this study offers practical implications for policymakers and institutional investors by showing how ESG integration can reduce risk exposure while enhancing long-term value creation.

title: Conceptual principles of forming the strategy of digital transformation of the national economy
summary: The article substantiates the conceptual foundations for developing a digital transformation strategy to advance the national economy. It has been established that digital transformation is a complex systemic process that goes beyond the implementation of digital technologies and encompasses structural, economic, organizational, institutional, and social changes aimed at increasing the productivity, competitiveness, and sustainability of the national economy. The evolution of scientific views on the concept of “digital transformation” is systematized, and the interrelated stages of digital transformations are distinguished: digitization, digitalization, and digital transformation. It was determined that the modern understanding of digital transformation is characterized by a transition from a technology-oriented approach to a systemic vision, in which digital technologies, data, innovations, and digital competences form the basis of the structural restructuring of economic and social processes. Modern scientific approaches to interpreting digital transformation are systematized, and the expediency of using a system-integrated approach at the level of the national economy, which combines technological, economic, organizational, institutional, and social components, is substantiated. It is proposed to consider the digital transformation of the national economy as a systematic, long-term, and managed process of structural-institutional and socio-economic transformation, based on digital technologies, data, innovation, and digital competences. The relationship between digital transformation and the development of the national economy is substantiated, which has a two-way nature: economic development forms the resource, institutional and personnel prerequisites for digital transformations, while digital transformation provides new opportunities for economic growth through increased productivity, stimulation of innovation, reduction of transaction costs, development of new markets and improvement of public administration efficiency. Keywords: digital transformation, digitalization, digital economy, national economy, development strategy, digital technologies, digital infrastructure.

title: Pengaruh ESG Disclosure, Green Investment, dan Eco-Efficiency terhadap Nilai Perusahaan: Studi pada Perusahaan Indeks IDX ESG Leaders (2020-2024)
summary: This study examines the effects of ESG disclosure, green investment, and eco-efficiency on the firm value of companies included in the IDX ESG Leaders Index, with 55 observations over the 2020–2024 period. Sustainability practices are increasingly drawing the attention of companies and investors because they are believed to enhance market confidence and firm value, although previous research has yielded inconsistent findings. A quantitative approach with a causal design was used in this study, utilizing secondary data. The sample was selected using purposive sampling, resulting in 11 companies as research subjects and 55 observations. The data were analyzed using panel data regression with the REM model. The results indicate that ESG Disclosure has a positive and significant effect on firm value, while Green Investment and Eco-Efficiency have negative and significant effects on firm value. Furthermore, all three variables have a significant simultaneous effect on firm value. These findings suggest that ESG disclosure receives a positive response from investors, whereas Green Investment and Eco-Efficiency have not yet fully created firm value, while also enriching the empirical evidence regarding the implementation of sustainability aspects within the Indonesian capital market.

title: Superior ESG performance and corporate R&D internationalization: evidence from China
summary: Purpose Amid intensifying global technological competition and shorter innovation cycles, R&D internationalization is critical for firms to optimize global innovation resource allocation. Meanwhile, growing demands for environmental governance and social inclusion have made sustainable business models an international consensus. Given China’s ESG context, establishing a credible ESG competitive advantage is pivotal to enhancing corporate R&D internationalization. Design/methodology/approach Using a sample of Chinese A share listed firms over 2009–2023, this study defines and measures superior ESG performance from a life cycle peer perspective, then examines its effect, mechanisms and contextual heterogeneity on corporate R&D internationalization. Findings First, superior ESG performance promotes the depth and breadth of corporate R&D internationalization. Second, it acts through four channels: increasing common ownership, facilitating digital transformation, alleviating investment-financing maturity mismatches and attracting analyst attention. Third, ESG disclosure, industry-finance cooperation and artificial intelligence policies strengthen the promotional effect of superior ESG performance on corporate R&D internationalization, reflecting positive policy synergy. Originality/value This study extends research on R&D internationalization determinants and fills the gap regarding the mechanisms of firm-level superior ESG performance. It also identifies the positive role of external institutional supply in emerging markets, offering practical implications for improving ESG systems and promoting R&D internationalization in developing economies similar to China.

title: The role of AI in advancing sustainable finance and environmental management impact: an analysis of leading construction firms on the London stock exchange
summary: Purpose The construction industry faces increasing pressure to align business practices with sustainable finance objectives and environmental responsibility. This study aims to investigate how major construction firms listed on the London Stock Exchange (LSE) disclose and position artificial intelligence (AI) technologies in relation to sustainable finance initiatives and environmental management practices. Design/methodology/approach Guided by the Resource-Based View (RBV) and Stakeholder Theory, the study employs qualitative content analysis of sustainability reports, ESG disclosures, and annual reports published between 2021 and 2024 by 23i LSE-listed construction firms. An iterative coding process was used to identify key themes and cross-case patterns relating to reported AI-enabled sustainability practices. Findings Four major themes emerged from the analysis: AI-driven environmental innovation; AI integration into sustainable finance mechanisms; strategic positioning and stakeholder communication of AI-enabled sustainability; and AI-supported environmental risk monitoring and compliance. The findings suggest that firms increasingly position AI as supporting environmental performance, sustainability reporting, stakeholder engagement, and sustainability-oriented governance. Cross-case analysis further revealed differences in the reported scope, maturity, and strategic framing of AI-enabled sustainability initiatives across firm categories, ranging from integrated systems to targeted applications, pilot initiatives, and future-oriented commitments. These differences are interpreted as indicative disclosure patterns rather than evidence of firm-size effects or independently verified differences in technological capability. Research limitations/implications This study advances scholarly understanding by demonstrating that AI reshapes traditional models of sustainable corporate strategy, underscoring the critical role of digital innovation at the intersection of environmental governance, financial accountability, and stakeholder engagement. Originality/value This study provides a novel perspective on the role attributed to AI within sustainability-oriented organisational contexts by examining how firms report and position AI in relation to environmental management, sustainable finance activities, and stakeholder communication. Rather than focusing solely on operational efficiency, the study highlights the strategic and communicative dimensions of AI within corporate sustainability narratives. The research provides empirical evidence relevant to RBV and Stakeholder Theory within the digitalisation context of the construction sector, while highlighting the importance of disclosure credibility, sustainability assurance, organisational legitimacy, and the potential for technology-enabled impression management.

title: Assessing the expected impact of logistics risks on supply chain performance
summary: Purpose This study develops an integrated framework that predicts logistics risks and quantifies their expected impact on supply chain performance. Existing research largely focuses on estimating risk occurrence but rarely evaluates both the likelihood and the potential consequences of disruptions. To address this gap, the study links machine learning (ML)-based risk prediction with an Expected Risk Impact (ERI) assessment to support more informed and impact-oriented decision-making. Design/methodology/approach The proposed framework combines Random Forest-based prediction of three logistics risks (customs risk, shipment delay risk and route disruption risk) with an ERI calculation derived by integrating predicted probabilities and independent severity measures. The analysis uses a real-world dataset of shipment operations in Southern California from 2021 to 2024. ERI distributions are examined to identify high-impact shipments, and coefficient-based interpretability techniques are applied to determine key risk drivers. Findings The results indicate that the models provide reliable risk probability estimates, while the ERI assessment reveals a highly skewed distribution of impacts, with a small subset of shipments accounting for disproportionately high expected risk exposure. Port congestion, handling operations, supplier reliability and route-related factors emerge as dominant contributors to high-impact risks. Practical implications The findings enable logistics managers to prioritize high-impact shipments, allocate resources more efficiently and design targeted mitigation strategies, thereby reducing operational disruptions and improving supply chain stability. Originality/value This study advances logistics risk management by bridging ML-based risk prediction with impact-oriented assessment. The integrated framework moves beyond occurrence-focused approaches and offers a more comprehensive basis for resilient supply chain decision support.

title: Pengaruh Mekanisme Good Corporate Governance terhadap Financial Statement Fraud dengan Audit Quality sebagai Variabel Moderasi pada Badan Usaha Milik Negara (BUMN) yang Terdaftar di BEI Periode 2020–2024
summary: Financial statement fraud is an act that can undermine the trust of shareholders and stakeholders in a company. Therefore, the implementation of Good Corporate Governance is necessary as a supervisory mechanism to minimize the likelihood of financial statement fraud. This study aims to analyze the influence of the Board of Commissioners (X1), the Audit Committee (X2), and Institutional Ownership (X3) on Financial Statement Fraud (Y), with Audit Quality (Z) as a moderating variable, in State-Owned Enterprises (SOEs) listed on the Indonesia Stock Exchange for the 2020–2024 period. Financial statement fraud is measured using the Beneish M-Score, while audit quality is measured based on the categories of Big Four and non-Big Four public accounting firms. This study employs a quantitative method using secondary data obtained from annual reports, audited financial statements, and corporate governance reports. The research sample was determined using purposive sampling, comprising 95 observations. Data analysis was conducted using panel data regression with the Random Effects Model and Moderated Regression Analysis (MRA) with the assistance of the EViews 12 software. The results indicate that the Board of Commissioners, the Audit Committee, and Institutional Ownership have a significant negative effect on Financial Statement Fraud. Furthermore, Audit Quality amplifies the negative effect of the Board of Commissioners, the Audit Committee, and Institutional Ownership on Financial Statement Fraud. In practical terms, this study contributes to state-owned enterprises by strengthening the implementation of good corporate governance and improving audit quality as a means of preventing financial statement fraud and enhancing corporate transparency and accountability.

title: Sustainable Finance and Carbon Pricing in Bioenergy Transition: A Contingent-Claim Approach to Renewable Energy Investment Under Land Constraints
summary: Biomass is widely recognized as a critical renewable energy source for supporting global decarbonization and energy diversification. However, the financial viability of bioenergy investments depends heavily on how climate policies and sustainable finance mechanisms interact under environmental uncertainty. This study develops a land-constrained bioenergy valuation model to examine the joint effects of carbon pricing, climate finance arrangements, and land-use regulations on the economic sustainability of biomass producers. Environmental and financial policies enter the framework through carbon costs, land-use constraints, and financial intermediation conditions, thereby linking climate regulation to firm-level capital performance. Using a contingent-claim framework, producer equity and financing risks are evaluated to capture the complex effects of market asset volatility on energy investment incentives. The framework is evaluated through a literature-informed baseline calibration and comparative-static numerical analysis; accordingly, the reported results are model-implied comparative-static mechanisms designed to evaluate bioenergy project viability under policy and market uncertainty. The numerical analysis employs a non-region-specific representative benchmark and is intended to identify structural and comparative-static mechanisms rather than to forecast outcomes for a particular geographical market. The results show that higher carbon prices reduce producer viability by increasing operating costs, although this financial strain is partially mitigated by the option-like nature of equity under higher asset volatility. In contrast, improvements in agronomic productivity, greater land availability, and higher biomass market prices enhance investment returns and financing conditions. The findings further indicate that climate policies shape bioenergy deployment not only through physical production costs but also through financial transmission channels and risk-sharing mechanisms. The study contributes to the energy policy and climate finance literature by integrating carbon pricing, land governance, and financial options within a unified analytical framework. The results highlight the importance of policy coordination between renewable energy incentives, sustainable finance management, and carbon regulation to mitigate investment risks in the bioenergy sector.

title: The Nexus Between Corporate Social Responsibility and Brand Loyalty Building Among Generation Z Consumers in Bayelsa State, Nigeria
summary: This study examines the effect of corporate social responsibility (CSR) on brand loyalty building among Generation Z consumers in Bayelsa State, Nigeria. Three dimensions of CSR community development initiatives, environmental responsibility, and ethical business practices are tested as independent predictors of Gen Z brand loyalty using simple regression analysis. Primary data were collected from 243 Gen Z consumers (born 1997–2012) in Yenagoa through a structured questionnaire. Results show that community development initiatives (β = 0.527, R² = 0.278, p < 0.01), environmental responsibility (β = 0.494, R² = 0.244, p < 0.01), and ethical business practices (β = 0.508, R² = 0.258, p < 0.01) each significantly predict Gen Z brand loyalty. These findings establish that CSR is not peripheral goodwill spending for firms targeting Generation Z in the Nigerian market but a strategically consequential driver of the loyalty that this digitally connected, values-driven, and socially conscious generation extends to brands that demonstrably act with purpose. The study contributes novel empirical evidence from a Gen Z-specific developing economy context and provides actionable strategic guidance for brand managers, CSR practitioners, and marketing policymakers.

title: Corporate Social Responsibility in Digitally Transformed Sports Ecosystems: How Empathy and Attitude Shape Sports Content Platform Usage
summary: As sports content platforms increasingly occupy a central role in consumers’ media consumption and fitness-related activities, understanding the factors that encourage sustained user engagement has become an important research concern. Although corporate social responsibility (CSR) has been widely recognized as a strategic tool for enhancing consumer perceptions and organizational reputation, prior research has focused primarily on traditional sports organizations and general commercial settings, with limited attention given to its influence within digitally mediated sports content platform environments. Therefore, this study investigates the relationships among CSR, empathy, attitude, and usage intention in the context of sports content platforms. Data were collected in Republic of Korea from 225 university students who regularly use sports content platforms. Structural equation modeling was employed to test the proposed conceptual framework. The findings reveal that CSR positively influences empathy and attitude, while empathy positively influences attitude. In addition, attitude is positively associated with usage intention. However, CSR does not directly influence usage intention, and empathy does not exhibit a direct relationship with usage intention. These results suggest that users’ continued engagement with sports content platforms is shaped more by evaluative attitudes than by direct emotional responses or perceptions of social responsibility alone. The study contributes to the literature by extending CSR research beyond traditional sports organizations into digitally transformed sports content platform environments and by identifying the psychological mechanisms through which CSR shapes user behavior in digital sports media environments. It also offers practical guidance for platform operators seeking to strengthen long-term user relationships through socially responsible initiatives.

title: The Impact of Digital Transformation on Corporate Environmental Performance: Empirical Evidence from China
summary: As digital transformation accelerates and the transition toward sustainable development intensifies, improving corporate environmental performance has become essential for achieving green and low-carbon development. However, limited attention has been paid to the multiple pathways through which digital transformation affects environmental performance and the conditions under which these effects occur. This study examines the impact of digital transformation on corporate environmental performance using an unbalanced panel of 2743 non-financial firms listed on the Shanghai and Shenzhen A-share stock exchanges in China from 2015 to 2024, yielding 14,163 firm–year observations. Firm and year fixed-effects models are employed to examine the causal relationship, its underlying mechanisms, and the moderating role of government subsidies, with extensive endogeneity and robustness tests conducted to assess the reliability of the findings. The findings show that digital transformation significantly improves corporate environmental performance through green technological innovation, resource allocation efficiency, media coverage, and analyst attention. Government subsidies further strengthen this relationship. Additional analyses reveal heterogeneous effects across firms with varying executive green cognition, CEO information technology backgrounds, and industry pollution intensity, while also providing evidence supportive of the Porter Hypothesis and consistent with the Matthew Effect regarding the simultaneous improvement in environmental and economic performance and the widening of inter-firm performance disparities, respectively. This study advances the literature on digital transformation and environmental governance by identifying the mechanisms, boundary conditions, and heterogeneous effects underlying this relationship, and provides practical implications for promoting corporate sustainability and green transition.

title: A person-centric dynamic view of responsible AI use: The role of behavioral signatures in supply chains
summary: As AI becomes increasingly embedded in supply chain operations, understanding how supply chain managers engage with these technologies in a responsible and context-sensitive manner is essential for advancing sustainable supply chain. Existing research tends to treat AI use as a trait-based phenomenon, overlooking the behavioral dynamics the same manager could exhibit across varied situations. This perspective article introduces the concept of the responsible AI use signature (RAI Signature), grounded in Cognitive-Affective Personality System theory (CAPS), to capture the stable yet dynamic patterns of responsible AI behavior demonstrated by the same manager across task, relational, and geographical contexts. A multi-level conceptual framework is developed to explain how RAI signature emerges and how it influences sustainable supply chain outcomes. Drawing on CAPS, this perspective article argues that RAI signature reflects the activation of cognitive-affective units in response to situational cues, moderated by individual, organizational, and technological factors. Three main propositions are developed to advance theory by shifting the focus from static competencies to within-person behavioral variability, offering a new lens for understanding, measuring, and developing managerial capacity in AI-enabled supply chains. This article contributes to research at the intersection of responsible AI, supply chain sustainability, and human-centered digital transformation.

title: Accounting Information and Firm Performance of Quoted Pharmaceutical Companies in Nigeria
summary: This study examined the effect of accounting information quality on the performance of quoted pharmaceutical companies in Nigeria. Accounting information quality was proxied by relevance, timeliness, and reliability, while firm performance was measured using return on equity (ROE). The study adopted an ex post facto research design and utilized secondary data obtained from the audited financial statements of pharmaceutical firms listed on the Nigerian Exchange Group over the period 2020–2024. Data were analyzed using descriptive statistics and the Ordinary Least Squares (OLS) regression technique. The findings revealed that accounting information quality significantly influences firm performance. Specifically, relevance and reliability exhibited positive and statistically significant effects on return on equity, while timeliness showed a weaker but significant relationship. The results indicate that improvements in the quality of financial reporting enhance firm performance and strengthen stakeholder confidence. The study concludes that the qualitative attributes of accounting information are critical drivers of firm performance and recommends that firms improve the relevance, timeliness, and reliability of financial reports to enhance financial outcomes.

title: Accelerating Digital Transformation in MSMEs: The Role of Digital Transformational Leadership, Agility, and Digital Literacy in DIY
summary: The study explores how Digital Transformational Leadership (DTL) influences the Digital Transformation (DT) of micro, small, and medium-sized enterprises (MSMEs), using dynamic capabilities theory and examining how Digital Literacy (DL) and Organizational Agility (OA) mediate these relationships. The research uses data from 241 MSMEs in the DIY region and applies a quantitative SEM-PLS methodology. Results show that DTL significantly and consistently influences DT both directly and indirectly through DL-OA. A mediation analysis indicates that both factors partially moderate the link between DTL and DT, with DL exerting a more pronounced mediating effect. The findings demonstrate that effective digital transformation in MSMEs hinges not only on exemplary leadership but also on employees' digital proficiency and the organization’s capacity for rapid adaptation. This study contributes to the growing body of scholarship by providing a cohesive theory that establishes a correlation between leadership behavior and transformational outcomes, grounded in dynamic capabilities and microfoundations. MSMEs should adopt a proactive strategy to develop digital competencies within their workforce and implement a more adaptable organizational structure to remain relevant and competitive in the rapidly changing digital environment.

title: Reviewing the ESG Investment and Financial Performance Literature: A Bibliometric and Systematic Review for Future Research
summary: ABSTRACT This study presents a thorough bibliometric and systematic review, devoted specifically to the literature concerned with the relationship between ESG investment and a firm's financial performance, by identifying crucial areas of future investigation. The paper presents a combined bibliometric and systematic literature review of 168 publications indexed in Scopus to cluster them into thematic groups, authors with the most impact, and geographical distribution with VOSviewer, and synthesize significant results of the literature on the area of corporate governance within ESG investment, performance, and ESG‐related regulatory and investment policy. Based on these findings, we suggest a TCCM framework that reveals the gaps in the theoretical perspective, methodological constraints, and sector‐specificities in ESG adoption in investment and corporate financial contexts. We find in our analysis that research is concentrated heavily in developed markets, that a variety of emerging regions are under‐represented, and that evidence on the financial benefits of ESG is mixed and usually context and measurement‐dependent. We end with specific recommendations of corporate governance within ESG investment to boards, regulators, and investors, and suggest a priority agenda for future empirical research. The article is relevant to ESG investment and financial‐performance research because it unites visual bibliometrics with formal SLR synthesis to inform scholarly and practitioner audiences. Existing literature on the review of ESG focuses solely on bibliometric trends or thematic discussions as independent analysis, where this paper combines bibliometric mapping, systematic synthesis of themes, and TCCM‐based structure to identify theoretical, contextual, and methodological gaps as an avenue for future ESG investment and financial‐performance research.

title: The impact of board digital cognition on the execution quality of corporate ESG strategy
summary: Against the background of deep integration between digital transformation and ESG governance, corporate ESG strategy no longer remains at the level of responsibility disclosure or image construction. It is gradually shifting toward target decomposition, resource allocation, process supervision, and performance improvement. As the core body of strategic decision-making and governance supervision, the board affects how firms understand ESG data, risk information, and execution processes through its level of digital cognition. Based on public disclosures of A-share non-financial listed companies from 2016 to 2023, the board digital cognition index can be constructed from directors' digital backgrounds, digital governance expressions, digital committee settings, and digital training disclosures. ESG strategy execution quality can be measured through target completion, quantitative disclosure, investment intensity, rating improvement, and penalty deductions. The baseline regression results show that board digital cognition has a significant positive effect on ESG strategy execution quality. The mechanism tests further show that internal control quality and digital investment strengthen this influence path. This finding indicates that board digital cognition not only reflects the upgrading of the governing body's knowledge structure, but also promotes the shift of ESG strategy from formal disclosure to substantive execution by improving information processing, supervisory constraints, and resource allocation.

title: Digital Transformation and Employee Adaptibility in IT Organizations
summary: Digital transformation has become one of the most important drivers of organizational growth and innovation in the Information Technology (IT) industry. It refers to the integration of advanced digital technologies into business processes, organizational operations, and decisionmaking to improve efficiency, productivity, customer experience, and business performance. Technologies such as Artificial Intelligence (AI), Cloud Computing, Big Data Analytics, Machine Learning, Robotic Process Automation (RPA), Internet of Things (IoT), Blockchain, and advanced collaboration platforms have significantly changed the way IT organizations operate. As organizations increasingly adopt digital technologies, employees are expected to continuously learn new skills, adapt to changing work environments, and embrace technological innovations. Employee adaptability has therefore become a critical factor in the success of digital transformation initiatives. Adaptability refers to an employees ability to learn new technologies, adjust to organizational changes, develop digital competencies, solve emerging challenges, and maintain high performance in dynamic work environments. Organizations that successfully support employee adaptability through training, leadership support, continuous learning, effective communication, and technology adoption achieve higher productivity, innovation, employee satisfaction, and long-term competitiveness. Digital transformation also improves operational efficiency by automating repetitive tasks, enabling real-time data analysis, enhancing collaboration, improving customer service, and supporting faster business decision-making. However, organizations also face challenges such as employee resistance to change, digital skill gaps, cybersecurity risks, technology integration complexity, increased workload during implementation, and concerns regarding job security. Human Resource Management and organizational leadership play a crucial role in facilitating successful digital transformation by providing learning opportunities, digital skill development programs, employee engagement initiatives, and effective change management strategies. title: MECHANISMS FOR EVALUATING THE PERFORMANCE OF MANAGERIAL STAFF IN THE CONTEXT OF CORPORATE GOVERNANCE
summary: This article provides a scientific examination of issues related to improving the mechanisms for evaluating the performance of managerial staff within the framework of corporate governance. The objective of the research is to analyze existing methods for evaluating managerial personnel in joint-stock companies and to develop an integrated approach aimed at enhancing theireffectiveness. The research methodology employed comparative analysis, statistical grouping, expert assessment, monographic study, as well as inductive and deductive methods; the financial and personnel indicators of Uzbekistan's joint-stock companies for 2021–2025 were used as empirical objects of analysis. The findings demonstrate that integrating financial indicatorsgrounded in agency theory with complex evaluation methods such as KPI, MBO, and 360-degree assessment significantly improves managerial staff performance and enhances the quality of management decisions. The scientific and practical significance of the work lies in the fact that the proposed integrated evaluation model enables the harmonious introduction of financial and nonfinancial indicators into national corporate governance practice and facilitates the formation of atransparent evaluation system for supervisory boards and executive bodies. The conclusions drawn serve as a source of practical recommendations for joint-stock companies, regulatory authorities, and academic researchers.

title: Turning ecology into economy: who provides biodiversity knowledge for institutional investors?
summary: Biodiversity is emerging as a material issue for institutional investors, driven by a growing concern for nature-related risks. This presents a challenge to the financial sector as institutional investors require metrics and tools to develop their investment strategies. Yet, biodiversity is not easily captured in standardized metrics. Therefore, new actors have emerged as knowledge providers. A question that remains unexamined is: which actors provide biodiversity expertise to the financial sector? Conducting a qualitative content analysis of investor reports, we highlight which actors have become knowledge producers in the field of biodiversity finance and what type of knowledge they introduce to the financial sector. We find that intergovernmental organizations, environmental NGOs, and member organizations are central to the communication of biodiversity loss to the financial sector. Additionally, we find that national research centers are taking on new, consultancy-like roles. Our findings highlight that, despite the emphasis on market actors in the social scientific scholarship of finance, the case of biodiversity finance draws attention to non-financial actors, in particular well-established ecological organizations, that are actively involved in turning ecology into economy.

title: Agents of collaborative adaptation: modelling temporal resilience in supply chains
summary: Abstract Supply-chain disruptions vary in intensity, scale, and frequency, producing temporally heterogeneous impacts on network viability. The emphasis on exposure and topology has anchored resilience in network structure, obscuring how collaboration and trust govern its phase-specific temporal dynamics, including resistive capabilities, adaptation speed, containment, and recovery. This study thus develops an agent-based simulation of the Netherlands logistics network, in which nodes operate as autonomous agents that redistribute load under capacity, link, and trust constraints. Cascading failures are simulated with trust-gated, capacity-aware, and collaboration-dependent load reallocation, capturing both immediate contagion and multi-step redistribution dynamics. The framework compares rule-based heuristics with adaptive AI agents trained using supervised imitation, online multiplicative adaptation, and cross-entropy policy search. Temporal resilience is then measured across each phase specific metrics of absorptive, adaptive, and recovery phases across the collaboration structure. This points to the main contribution of this article, in which AI agents improve adaptation and cascade containment through targeted use of high-trust, high-capacity links, while recovery dynamics remain bounded by structural and exogenous constraints. This points to a layered view of resilience, where performance depends on the interaction between network configuration, trust-mediated coordination, and agent-level adaptation.

title: The Effect of Board of Directors and Audit Committee Characteristics on Financial Reporting Quality: Evidence from Consumer Non-Cyclicals Companies Listed on the Indonesia Stock Exchange, 2022–2025
summary: The research evaluates the effect of board of directors and audit committee characteristics on the quality of financial reporting in consumer non-cyclicals companies listed on the Indonesia Stock Exchange (IDX) during 2022–2025. The research is motivated by concerns regarding the quality of financial reporting and the potential for managerial opportunistic behavior through managerial earnings manipulation. Therefore, this study aims to empirically analyze whether board size, board gender diversity, and audit committee size influence the quality of financial reporting. A quantitative causal-comparative approach was employed using secondary data obtained from companies’ annual reports and financial statements. The sample was selected using purposive sampling, and panel data regression was applied to test the partial and simultaneous effects of the independent variables. Financial reporting quality was proxied by discretionary accruals measured using the Modified Jones Model. The the estimates suggest that board size has a negative and significant effect on discretionary accruals, suggesting that a larger board of directors is related to lower managerial earnings manipulation and, consequently, higher the quality of financial reporting. In contrast, board gender diversity has no significant effect on discretionary accruals. Audit committee size also does not have a significant effect at the 5% significance level. Overall, the findings indicate that board size plays a more significant role in improving the quality of financial reporting than board gender diversity and audit committee size.

title: Building centrality in critical supply chains : the case of phosphates
summary: Phosphate is a critical input in agricultural supply chains, yet major phosphate-producing countries vary considerably in how far they have moved beyond the extraction and export of raw phosphate rock toward the domestic production of higher-value fertilizers. Over the past two decades, Morocco has captured a substantial share of the phosphate fertilizer market and moved downstream more rapidly than larger and more established mining producers (e.g. US, Brazil, Australia…) despite not possessing their economic scale and longstanding mining expertise. This puzzling story leads to the question: How can resource-producing states use state-linked firms to move downstream in critical supply chains, and why are some more successful than others? Building on the literature on resource linkage, global value chains and industrial policy, I argue that downstream upgrading depends on the interaction of three processes: the capacity and strategic orientation of state-linked firms to sustain long-term investments; targeted investment that connects successive stages of production; and foreign partnership that strengthen technological capabilities, market access, distribution networks, and knowledge of customer demand. I develop this argument through a process-tracing analysis of Morocco’s phosphate industry and a structured comparison with Saudi Arabia and Jordan, drawing from trade and production data, annual reports and news coverage in English, Arabic and French. The comparison demonstrates that large natural endowments, large-scale investment, and foreign partnerships are not sufficient on their own to produce downstream upgrading. Their effects depend on how they are coordinated and strategically directed to expand domestic value-added production. This study contributes to scholarship on resource-based industrialization, industrial policy, global value chains, and phosphate and fertilizer supply chains.

title: Exploring the role of digital innovation in advancing supply chain sustainability through inventory management in the Malaysian retail sector
summary: Digital innovation is progressively transforming the way organizations handle supply chain operations, especially with the use of technologies like artificial intelligence, cloud computing, blockchain, and the Internet of Things (IoT). Specifically, the objectives of this study are to identify the factors shaping digital innovation adoption in inventory management and analyse how inventory visibility conditions the sustainability value of such innovation. A qualitative basic inquiry design was employed, using semi-structured interviews with twelve managers directly involved in inventory-related decision-making, including retail, warehouse, finance, and transportation managers. Data were analysed thematically through manual coding. The results indicate that the adoption of digital innovation for some organizations depends on the economic performance of their business. The research also reveals that digital innovation can improve supply chain sustainability through waste reduction, cost efficiency, and supply stability, but only when supported by organizational readiness and transparent information sharing. This result reinforces the holistic view that digital transformation is a socio-organizational process and is not subject to technical considerations alone. Inventory management is not merely an internal technical activity but also a practical mechanism, namely the ability to implement digital innovation, which demonstrates effectiveness in supporting sustainable supply chain outcomes.

title: Theoretical foundations of hr in the digital economy and transformation of enterprise human capital management mechanisms
summary: The article advances the theoretical foundations of HR functioning in the digital economy and substantiates the transformation of enterprise human capital management mechanisms. It is argued that HR digitalization should not be reduced to the automation of personnel administration, recruitment, or training, since its economic significance lies in changing how human capital is formed, utilized, developed, and reproduced. The distinctions between electronic, digital, and intelligent HR management are clarified. The roles of data, HR analytics, artificial intelligence, cloud platforms, and employee self-service in the shift from reactive personnel procedures to predictive and strategic management are revealed. The principles of digital HR transformation are systematized as follows: strategic alignment, human-centeredness, evidence-based decision-making, adaptability, ethics, algorithmic transparency, data security, and continuous organizational learning. A theoretical architecture of HR in the digital economy is proposed, combining digital infrastructure, redesigned HR processes, analytical and competency components, and strategic outcomes. A mechanism for the transition from the traditional to the digital model of human capital management is developed. It includes assessing digital maturity, creating a data architecture, redesigning processes, developing digital competencies and culture, evaluating effects, and continuous improvement. The study demonstrates that the effectiveness of digital HR is determined not by the number of implemented technologies but by their integration with enterprise strategy, organizational culture, trust mechanisms, and the economic objectives of human capital development. The proposed provisions form a methodological basis for further diagnosis of digital HR maturity and for designing enterprise-specific transformation programs. title: Effect of Culture on Financial Reporting Quality of Listed Conglomerate Companies in Nigeria
summary: This study examines the effect of cultural dimensions; uncertainty avoidance, long-term orientation, and organizational culture on the financial reporting quality (FRQ) of listed conglomerate companies in Nigeria. The study adopts an ex post facto research design using panel data from six listed conglomerate firms over a ten-year period (2015–2024), resulting in 60 firm year observations. Data were analyzed using panel regression techniques, including pooled OLS, fixed effects, and random effects models, with the Hausman test confirming the suitability of the random effects model. Robust estimation techniques were employed to address heteroskedasticity and serial correlation issues. The findings revealed that uncertainty avoidance has a positive and statistically significant effect on financial reporting quality, indicating that risk-averse environments enhance reporting reliability and transparency. Organizational culture also exhibits a positive and significant effect, suggesting that firms with strong ethical, adaptive, and transparent cultures produce higher quality financial reports. However, long-term orientation shows a positive but statistically insignificant relationship with financial reporting quality, implying that its influence is context-dependent and not sufficiently strong within the study period. The study concludes that while national cultural dimensions contribute to financial reporting practices, organizational culture is the most influential factor in improving financial reporting quality among listed conglomerate companies in Nigeria. The study recommends strengthening internal control systems, promoting ethical corporate cultures, integrating long-term reporting strategies, and enhancing regulatory oversight to improve reporting quality.

title: The effects of ESG activities on firm performance: evidence from the BRICS
summary: Purpose This study aims to analyze the individual effects of environmental, social and governance (ESG) components on the performance of companies from BRICS countries (Brazil, Russia, India, China and South Africa) during the period from 2010 to 2023. Design/methodology/approach The sample consists of 12,750 companies from 2010 to 2023. A multilevel regression model was employed to capture the influence of variables at different analytical levels. Findings The results reveal that practices related to emissions management, diversity, inclusion and employee well-being have positive and significant impacts on return on assets and return on equity. Corporate governance, especially shareholder protection mechanisms, also proved to be a key factor in improving performance. On the other hand, investments in innovation and resource use showed negative effects on short-term performance. It was observed that larger firms face greater challenges in converting ESG practices into immediate market value. Practical implications The paper provides insights for managers by reinforcing the strategic importance of integrating ESG practices, particularly those related to human capital and governance, to enhance firm performance. The findings also offer practical implications for investors by identifying ESG dimensions associated with sustainable corporate growth in BRICS countries. Social implications The study highlights the role of diversity and employee well-being in promoting more equitable corporate environments, reinforcing sustainability as a driver of organizational transformation in emerging markets. Originality/value The originality of the study lies in the combination of a multilevel approach with a comparative analysis among emerging economies, filling gaps in the literature on corporate sustainability in developing countries.

title: Conceptual and applied elements of the digital transformation of the national economy and the development of ukraine’s ict sector
summary: The article examines the conceptual and applied elements of the digital transformation of the national economy and the realization of the potential of Ukraine’s information and communication technology (ICT) sector. It substantiates the need to develop an integrated state policy framework that combines institutional, organizational, economic, technological, and innovation instruments to support comprehensive digital modernization. The study identifies the key strategic priorities of digital transformation, including the development of resilient digital infrastructure, modernization of public administration and digital public services, digitalization of key economic sectors, strengthening cybersecurity and digital sovereignty, development of digital skills and human capital, and expansion of Ukraine’s integration into the European and global digital space. Particular attention is devoted to the ICT sector as the principal driver of technological modernization, digital innovation, and the formation of a competitive digital ecosystem. The paper argues that the effectiveness of digital transformation depends on strategic coordination between national digital development priorities and policies to strengthen the ICT sector. A system of conceptual provisions is proposed that integrates sectoral digitalization, technological modernization, digital governance, cybersecurity, human capital development, innovation support, and international technological cooperation into a unified framework for state regulation. It is demonstrated that implementing these interconnected strategic priorities will create favorable institutional and technological conditions for sustainable economic development, strengthen the resilience of critical infrastructure, reduce technological dependence on external markets, stimulate innovation, and enhance the international competitiveness of the Ukrainian economy. Under the conditions of full-scale war and post-war recovery, the proposed conceptual framework can serve as a methodological basis for shaping an effective state policy of digital transformation, ensuring technological sovereignty, accelerating economic modernization, and facilitating Ukraine’s integration into the European and global digital and innovation ecosystem. title: Corporate Governance and the Sustainability of Igbo-Owned Small and Medium Enterprises in Nigeria
summary: The effect of corporate governance on the sustainability of Igbo-owned Small and Medium Enterprises (SMEs) in Nigeria is examined. Although these enterprises contribute significantly to employment generation, economic growth, and entrepreneurial development, they face high failure rates primarily due to internal structural weaknesses, notably the absence of formal governance systems. A qualitative and conceptual research design is adopted, utilizing a systematic review and synthesis of recent empirical and theoretical literature (2022–2025). Agency Theory, Stakeholder Theory, and the Resource-Based View inform the exploration of how governance mechanisms—such as accountability, transparency, ownership structure, stakeholder engagement, and ethical practices—influence business survival, financial performance, and long term sustainability. The findings indicate that, while Igbo-owned SMEs possess strong entrepreneurial capacity rooted in indigenous practices like the apprenticeship system, their sustainability is compromised by informality, inadequate record-keeping, lack of succession planning, and centralized decision-making. The study establishes that effective corporate governance enhances organizational resilience, strengthens stakeholder trust, facilitates access to finance, and supports strategic decision-making. Nevertheless, the adoption of governance practices remains limited due to cultural, structural, and institutional constraints. The study concludes that integrating formal corporate governance mechanisms with indigenous entrepreneurial systems is critical to improving the sustainability of Igbo-owned SMEs. It recommends actions such as formalizing business structures, offering capacity building, planning for succession, improving financial management systems, and enacting supportive regulatory frameworks. The study contributes to the literature by providing context-specific insights into governance practices within indigenous entrepreneurial settings. It also offers practical implications for policymakers, SME operators, and development agencies.

title: Leveraging Digital Transformation For Knowledge Management In Projects
summary: This paper investigates how Digital Transformation (DT) influences Knowledge Management (KM) within Project Management (PM) environments. Guided by grounded theory, the study employed twenty semi-structured interviews with project managers. Data were analysed using ATLAS.ti through open, axial, and selective coding. The analysis generated a conceptual model explaining how DT influences KM through four interrelated categories: facilitators, enablers, limiters, and disablers. Findings show that DT enhances knowledge capture, transfer, and application, although its effectiveness depends on organisational readiness and governance. Facilitators reflect contextual and behavioural conditions for DT-supported KM, while enablers operationalise this readiness. Limiters reduce DT effectiveness, whereas disablers represent structural or systemic barriers that may block integration. Theoretically, the study proposes a mechanism-oriented framework that extends DT, KM, and PM research beyond technology-centric explanations. Practically, it supports managers in strengthening organisational readiness, aligning governance, mitigating barriers, and leveraging DT to improve organisational learning and project performance.

title: Interpretable and leakage-aware prediction of shipment delays in global supply chains: a Random Forest–SHAP workflow with multi-model benchmarking on the DataCo dataset
summary: Purpose This study develops a leakage-aware evaluation workflow for predicting shipment dispatch delays at the time of order, auditing when each predictor becomes available and quantifying how much apparent accuracy on the DataCo dataset derives from post-outcome information. Design/methodology/approach On 172,765 completed DataCo shipments, a point-in-time audit identifies 21 order-time features and excludes post-outcome fields, including Late_delivery_risk. Five identically tuned models are compared over 15 order-grouped resamples with Nadeau–Bengio corrected t-tests (Holm-adjusted), cluster-bootstrap intervals, a chronological split, and exact SHapley Additive exPlanations (SHAP). Findings The leakage-free Random Forest attains R2 = 0.2719 (95% confidence interval 0.2569–0.2864). Restoring post-outcome fields raises R2 to 0.7589: a leakage inflation of ΔR2 = +0.4870 (same model, with versus without post-outcome inputs). A distinct diagnostic, the leaky model’s margin over a flag-threshold rule (ΔR2 = +0.0951), is meaningful only conditional on the leak. All five honest models lie within 0.0084 R2; SHAP indicates that order-time delay risk is structural, driven by mode, lane, and category base rates. Research limitations/implications Findings derive from one public dataset whose target is dispatch (not delivery) delay; generalisability claims are correspondingly modest. Practical implications Delay largely reflects infeasible service-level promises; the managerial levers are promise recalibration and base-rate triage, with measured detection rates (precision 0.864, recall 0.553) separated from assumed costs. Originality/value A feature-level point-in-time audit, a quantification of leakage inflation on a widely used benchmark, and a replicable leakage-audit protocol including a target-permutation canary.

title: Does Green Finance Reform Promote Corporate Long-Term Investment? Evidence from China
summary: We study the effects of green finance reform on firms’ long-term investment using data from a Chinese green finance pilot policy introduced in 2017 and panel data on listed firms covering an eleven-year period. We find that the policy significantly increases long-term investment, with the effect accounting for approximately 17.86% of the sample mean. This positive effect mainly operates by easing firms’ financing constraints, improving firms’ financing maturity structure, and mitigating uncertainty at both the operational and market levels. Heterogeneity analyses reveal that the policy effect is more pronounced among mature firms, non-state-owned enterprises, firms with financially experienced directors, supervisors, and senior managers, and those in non-pollution-intensive industries and competitive markets.

title: Explainable AI in Supply Chain Management: Opportunities and Research Challenges
summary: The rapid adoption of Artificial Intelligence (AI) in Supply Chain Management (SCM) has transformed traditional decision-making processes by enabling predictive analytics, demand forecasting, inventory optimization, supplier evaluation, logistics planning, and risk management. Despite the significant performance improvements achieved through AI-driven systems, the increasing reliance on complex machine learning and deep learning models has raised concerns regarding transparency, trustworthiness, accountability, and regulatory compliance. Many advanced AI models operate as “black boxes,” making it difficult for supply chain managers and stakeholders to understand how decisions are generated. Consequently, Explainable Artificial Intelligence (XAI) has emerged as a promising solution to enhance transparency and interpretability while maintaining the predictive power of AI systems. This paper presents a comprehensive review and conceptual analysis of Explainable AI in Supply Chain Management, examining its opportunities, applications, challenges, and future research directions. The study synthesizes findings from recent literature published between 2018 and 2026 and critically evaluates the role of XAI across major supply chain functions, including demand forecasting, procurement, supplier selection, inventory management, transportation, sustainability monitoring, and risk mitigation. The paper further identifies key barriers to XAI implementation, including data quality issues, model complexity, scalability concerns, organizational resistance, and the lack of standardized evaluation frameworks. A conceptual framework is proposed to illustrate how explainability can improve decision quality, stakeholder trust, operational resilience, and sustainable supply chain performance. The findings indicate that organizations integrating explainable AI mechanisms into supply chain analytics are better positioned to achieve transparency, regulatory compliance, and collaborative decision-making. The paper contributes to both theory and practice by establishing a research agenda that addresses emerging technological, managerial, and sustainability-related challenges associated with Explainable AI adoption in modern supply chains. title: The role of artificial intelligence in enhancing global supply chain efficiency
summary: Данная работа посвящена изучению того, как технологии искусственного интеллекта (ИИ) могут повысить эффективность глобальных цепочек поставок, а также разработке практических рекомендаций для компаний, планирующих их внедрение, особенно на развивающихся рынках. В ходе исследования были поставлены следующие задачи: 1. Был проведен обзор существующей литературы по применению ИИ в управлении цепочками поставок, проанализированы два практических кейса — компании Siemens (прогностическое техническое обслуживание) и RIDA Group в Судане (цепочка поставок в горнодобывающей отрасли), — а также разработана дорожная карта внедрения, состоящая из трех этапов. 2. Анализ показал, что ИИ способен сократить расходы на техническое обслуживание примерно на 25%, уменьшить время простоя оборудования и повысить устойчивость цепочки поставок. Для RIDA Group предложенная дорожная карта включает пилотный этап, этап масштабирования и создание полномасштабной экосистемы; ожидаемая окупаемость инвестиций составляет около 52% за два года. 3. Полученные результаты могут быть полезны компаниям из аналогичных отраслей, особенно на развивающихся рынках, планирующим внедрение ИИ в процессы управления цепочками поставок. Работа была выполнена на базе Санкт-Петербургского политехнического университета Петра Великого с использованием как теоретических исследований, так и анализа практических примеров для формирования комплексного представления о применении ИИ в управлении цепочками поставок. Исследование включало анализ отраслевых проблем и разработку стратегической дорожной карты внедрения из трех этапов, адаптированной для развивающихся рынков, с особым акцентом на горнодобывающую и производственную сферы. Итогом исследования стал набор практических рекомендаций и стратегических подходов, которые могут взять на вооружение компании, стремящиеся повысить устойчивость своих цепочек поставок и операционную эффективность с помощью технологий ИИ. title: Artificial intelligence – driven digital finance and green innovation: evidence from India
summary: Purpose This study looks at the relationship between corporate green innovation, digital finance, and artificial intelligence (AI) in Indian listed companies. It also looks at whether digital finance makes the relationship between AI intensity and green innovation stronger. Design/methodology/approach Pooled ordinary least squares and two-way fixed-effects models are used to account for firm- and year-specific heterogeneity in an unbalanced panel of 5,740 firm-year data for Indian listed enterprises between 2012 and 2024. Robustness analyses evaluate how stable the results are. Findings Across model specifications, corporate green innovation is positively and significantly correlated with AI intensity. A one-standard-deviation rise in AI intensity is linked to a roughly 1.1% increase in green innovation in the favored two-way fixed-effects model, suggesting a small but significant economic impact. By facilitating better access to financial resources for sustainable initiatives, digital finance reinforces this beneficial correlation. The findings should be taken as associations rather than causal effects because of the observational research approach. Practical implications Encouraging responsible AI use in conjunction with digital financial infrastructure may improve businesses' ability for green innovation and reduce funding barriers for sustainable investments. Originality/value The paper advances knowledge of the joint relationship between AI, digital finance, and corporate green innovation in an emerging country by presenting firm-level evidence from India and combining technological and financial viewpoints.

title: Pengaruh Profitabilitas dan Leverage terhadap Nilai Perusahaan dengan Pengungkapan Corporate Social Responsibility sebagai Variabel Moderasi pada Perusahaan Nonbank yang Terdaftar dalam Indeks LQ45 Periode 2020–2024
summary: This study aims to examine the effect of profitability and leverage on firm value with corporate social responsibility disclosure as a moderating variable. The population comprises non-bank companies listed in the LQ45 Index for the 2020–2024 period, and 26 companies with 130 observations were selected through purposive sampling. Profitability is proxied by return on assets, leverage by the debt to assets ratio, firm value by Tobin's Q, and corporate social responsibility by the corporate social responsibility disclosure index based on the Global Reporting Initiative standards. The data are secondary data obtained from annual reports and sustainability reports, and they were analysed using panel data regression with a moderated regression analysis approach through EViews 10. Model selection using the Chow test, the Hausman test, and the Lagrange Multiplier test resulted in the common effect model. The results show that, simultaneously, the model is statistically fit, but partially profitability does not significantly affect firm value, leverage does not significantly affect firm value, and corporate social responsibility disclosure has no significant direct effect on firm value. Corporate social responsibility disclosure is also not proven to moderate the effect of either profitability or leverage on firm value. The adjusted coefficient of determination of 23.47 percent indicates that most of the variation in firm value is explained by factors outside the model.

title: Digital transformation of sanitary and epidemiological monitoring: the case of Kazakhstan
summary: Introduction This study examines the digital transformation of sanitary and epidemiological monitoring in Kazakhstan and identifies managerial mechanisms supporting timely, coordinated, and data-driven public health responses. Methods The study combines a two-tier comparative analysis of benchmark countries and regional institutional comparators with regulatory review, institutional analysis, digital maturity assessment, national indicators for 2019–2023, and expert evaluation. Results The analysis identifies fragmented interagency coordination, outdated regulatory arrangements, and uneven regional digital capacity as major constraints. An adapted digital maturity index and an institutional–digital model based on platform integration, legal modernization, and behavioral sensitivity are proposed. Discussion The findings indicate that stronger coordination, clearer managerial KPIs, and integrated digital infrastructure may improve the diagnostic readiness of sanitary monitoring. The proposed model should be regarded as a diagnostic and conceptual framework requiring further empirical validation.

title: Navigating IoT failure risks in healthcare digital transformation: strategic implications for private and public hospitals
summary: Purpose Against the backdrop of healthcare's ongoing digital transformation as a pivotal industry trend, this paper aims to explore Internet of Things (IoT) technology's role in driving this shift while investigating how potential risks stemming from technology failures shape investment decisions. We focus on analyzing the decision-making mechanisms of both public and private hospitals regarding IoT adoption, shedding light on how technology failure risks influence their strategic choices in pursuing digital transformation initiatives. Design/methodology/approach This paper employs game theory to examine public and private hospitals' IoT adoption decisions, explicitly incorporating the risk of IoT technology failures. Based on a dynamic game framework, we investigate how three key factors – initial medical service utility, mismatch costs and reimbursement ratios – impact competitive healthcare market, patient preference improvement and benefit/profit enhancement across scenarios where public and private hospitals act as market pioneers or followers. Findings Our findings underscore the critical role of strategic IoT adoption decisions in the competitive healthcare landscape, highlighting how IoT implementation success probabilities and patient care mismatch costs directly impact hospitals' profitability and broader social welfare – specifically by shaping resource allocation efficiency and service accessibility. The results reveal that public and private hospitals should tailor their strategies to their inherent strengths (e.g. public hospitals' policy alignment, private hospitals' flexibility), relevant reimbursement policies and expected IoT success rates to optimize outcomes. Furthermore, we emphasize the necessity of incorporating external contextual factors – including stakeholder dynamics, socioeconomic contexts and the specificity of IoT-enabled healthcare services – into strategic decision-making, as these variables modulate the trade-offs between technology risks and transformation benefits for both hospital types. Originality/value This research delivers significant insights for both academia and practice, providing actionable recommendations to optimize the procurement and utilization of IoT services in the healthcare supply chain.

title: Optimization of military property accounting as a factor of strengthening the financial sustainability of the afu: a paradigm of digital forensics
summary: The article examines the optimization of military property accounting as a factor in strengthening the financial resilience of the Armed Forces of Ukraine under martial law and the digital transformation of the security and defense sector. Reliability and traceability of accounting information are considered prerequisites for effective asset management and internal control. The study identifies risks that arise at the main stages of the military asset life cycle, including recognition, storage, movement, transfer to operation, repair, inventory, write-off, and adjustment of accounting data. The methodology combines systems, risk-oriented, process, and information-analytical approaches with analysis, synthesis, and structural-functional modeling. The Digital Military Forensics Framework (DMFF) is further developed by integrating it with the Military Asset Financial Resilience (MAFR) model. The integrated DMFF–MAFR model combines military property accounting, formation of an asset’s digital trace, Big Data analytics, risk indicators, anomaly detection, internal control, internal audit, and managerial response. The study substantiates the relationship among accounting information quality, asset traceability, property loss reduction, efficient resource use, and financial resilience. A system of digital forensics risk indicators is proposed to identify unusual transactions and deviations requiring professional review. An individual risk indicator is treated not as evidence of a violation but as an analytical signal for further examination. The scientific novelty lies in integrating digital forensics with military property accounting, internal control, and internal audit through continuous analysis of an asset’s digital trace throughout its life cycle. The proposed approach shifts the emphasis from predominantly retrospective control to continuous risk-oriented monitoring and early detection of potential problems. Its practical application can improve accounting reliability and asset traceability, rationalize control and audit resources, reduce potential property losses, strengthen financial security, and enhance accountability in the use of defense resources. title: Equity Valuation and Financial Reporting in the Manufacturing Sector ln Nigeria
summary: This study examined the impact of equity valuation metrics — Price-to-Book ratio, Price-toEarnings ratio, and Dividend Yield — on financial reporting comparability and transparency among listed manufacturing firms in Nigeria. Using a quantitative ex-post facto design, the study analysed panel data from 15 NGX-listed manufacturing companies from 2016–2025. Comparability was measured using the Barth et al. (2012) accounting system comparability score, while transparency was proxied by the FRC Nigeria disclosure index. OLS and fixed-effects regression results indicated that P/B ratio and Dividend Yield had a statistically significant positive relationship with both comparability and transparency, whereas P/E ratio showed a weaker, context-dependent association. The findings suggested that firms with higher marketbased valuations were incentivized to provide higher quality disclosures to sustain investor confidence in Nigeria’s volatile macroeconomic environment. The study recommended that the Financial Reporting Council mandate standardized valuation-related disclosures to reduce information asymmetry.

title: IOT-Enabled FKF–FKL Spectral Analysis for Intelligent and Resilient Supply Chains
summary: Modern multi-echelon supply chains generate heterogeneous Internet of Things (IoT) telemetry containing lead-time fluctuations, irregular sampling, transportation delays, intensity variations, and operational disruptions. This study proposes an FKF–FKL spectral framework for constrained resilience analysis that separates observational effects from genuine structural change. Fourier analysis captures temporal dynamics, while the Kontorovich–Lebedev (FKL) representation characterizes scale-dependent behavior. Shift-invariant properties distinguish temporal displacement from structural change, whereas exponential modulation and spectral differentials characterize intensity variation and localized disruptions. A distributional formulation on a testing-function space accommodates irregular IoT observations, and sequential convergence of the two-sided FKF transform supports continuous spectral-state updating inside digital twins. Compact spectral features feed resilience scoring, AI-based decision-making, green logistics and sustainable mobility planning, hash-chain (blockchain) provenance, and hybrid quantum-classical logistics optimization (quantum annealing / QUBO). The framework provides an interpretable route for detecting and classifying disturbances across procurement, production, warehousing, unit-load-device handling, and intelligent transportation systems under Industry 5.0 human-centric automation. title: Green Finance and SME Growth in Morocco: The Mediating Role of Green Investment
summary: This study examines the impact of green finance on SME growth by incorporating green investment as a mediating variable within the context of Moroccan SMEs. Drawing on the Resource-Based View (RBV), the study explains how access to environmentally oriented financial resources may stimulate sustainable investment practices and contribute to organizational growth. A quantitative survey approach was employed, and data were collected from 116 Moroccan SMEs through a self-administered questionnaire administered to business owners and managers. The data were analyzed using structural equation modeling with the partial least squares (SEM-PLS) technique under R software. The results indicate that green finance has a positive and significant effect on green investment. In addition, green investment positively and significantly influences SME growth, while the direct effect of green finance on SME growth remains relatively limited. The mediation analysis confirms that green investment partially mediates the relationship between green finance and SME growth. These findings highlight the strategic importance of environmentally sustainable investments as a transmission mechanism through which green finance may contribute to SME development and competitiveness in emerging economies.

title: Economic security of the enterprise under corporate governance: conceptualization and correlation with corporate security
summary: The rapid development of Ukraine’s corporate sector underscores the need to theoretically distinguish between “economic security of the enterprise” and “corporate security,” which, in the scholarly literature, are largely treated as synonyms despite substantive differences. The relevance of the study stems from terminological uncertainty that complicates the practical delineation of authority and responsibility between an enterprise’s financial-economic units and its corporate security units. The article aims to conceptualize the relationship between the enterprise’s economic security and corporate security within corporate governance, to develop a mechanism for distinguishing between them, and to refine the corresponding terminology. The study employs the systems approach, the comparative method, content analysis of scholarly sources, and methods of classification and generalization. Scholarly approaches to interpreting economic and corporate security of the enterprise have been systematized; a mechanism for distinguishing them has been developed across six criteria – the object of protection, scope of coverage, responsible subject, dominant instruments, theoretical origin of the concept, and type of correlation; refined definitions of economic security of the enterprise and corporate security have been proposed, explicitly stating their hierarchical correlation under corporate governance. The practical significance lies in the applicability of the results to the delineation of functional responsibilities between enterprise units responsible for financial-economic and corporate security. The novelty lies in developing a criteria-based mechanism for distinguishing the enterprise’s economic security from corporate security, which, unlike existing approaches that merely state the broader scope of corporate security, enables unambiguous classification of specific managerial decisions and threats as belonging to either subsystem. Prospects for further research include developing a mechanism to ensure the enterprise’s economic security under corporate governance, based on the proposed distinction. title: Digital Transformation and Firm Performance: The Moderating Role of CFO Co-optation
summary: Purpose: This study tests whether digital transformation affects firm accounting performance in Indonesian manufacturing firms, and whether Chief Financial Officer (CFO) co-optation moderates that effect.Research Methodology: This study analyzes 285 firm-year observations from 95 Indonesia Stock Exchange manufacturing firms (2022–2024) using Fixed Effects panel regression with Moderated Multiple Regression, applying one-tailed significance tests at the 10%, 5%, and 1% levels. The study measures digital transformation through text-mining keyword frequency in annual reports and codes CFO co-optation as a binary indicator for CFO appointment during the sitting Chief Executive Officer (CEO) tenure. The study estimates a Fixed Effects panel regression in Stata 17, selected through Chow and Hausman tests, with Moderated Multiple Regression testing the interaction effect.Results: Digital transformation lowers Return on Assets at the 10% significance level. CFO co-optation lowers ROA at the 5% level, but the interaction between digital transformation and CFO co-optation raises ROA at the 5% level, offsetting and reversing the direct penalty.Conclusions: Executive alignment through CFO co-optation buffers the short-term cost digital transformation imposes on profitability, consistent with Resource Orchestration Theory operating alongside Agency Theory rather than replacing it.Limitations: The sample covers manufacturing firms only, over a three-year window, using a keyword-based digital transformation proxy.Contributions: The findings extend Agency Theory and Resource Orchestration Theory into a joint governance-technology model and offer Indonesian regulators, boards, and CFOs concrete guidance on staffing and timing digital transformation initiatives.
